items.title: David Torkanowsky interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, September 26, 2019
items.q: the best that I’ve ever heard, besides Jimmy Rowles and the old guys, is Mulgrew Miller.

ctx.x: And it’s a very, very intimate relationship. Like just when they’re singing out of time it’s like you start to learn to listen for the mouth opening because you know they’re about to go [sings] I — and you know where the down beat is. So it’s a very, you know the best that I’ve ever heard, besides Jimmy Rowles and the old guys, is Mulgrew Miller. He was so good, he was so good at it. Billy Childs was really great at it. You know there’s a lot of great accompanists. I was never on that level. But I could always…
You had a little anecdote about on the radio thing playing behind David Bartholomew and he was playing “Body and Soul” and he — it sounded to me like maybe he dropped a beat here and there.
